key_insight: PAINT is a multilingual framework that standardizes how pain is identified and represented across medical exams and real-world clinical text in four languages.
clinical_relevance: It can help improve pain extraction from diverse documentation, supporting more consistent symptom understanding across multilingual healthcare settings.
method: Built nine pain-focused dataset partitions spanning English, Spanish, Portuguese, and Japanese.
Created a structured annotation schema for pain relevance, pain presence, location, descriptors, and demographics.
Used LLMs with an ensemble approach, then validated labels with ten clinicians.
evidence_signal: The ensemble achieved macro-F1 of 0.91–1.00 for pain relevance and pain presence, 92–100% accuracy for demographics, and inter-annotator κ of 0.82–1.00.
watch_item: Performance was validated on curated/licensed corpora, so generalization to other institutions, note styles, or lower-resource settings may still need local testing.
paper_title: PAINT: A Framework for Multilingual Pain Representation from Medical Licensing Exams to Real-World Clinical Texts
